hw.rule_time: It closes itself after 30 days, or by hand. Opening it needs a reason, a step-up and a cutoff date that is not in the future.

Own save, reason and audit row.

dr.title: Reset the project data

dr.rule_expiry: A request expires after {{minutes}} minutes; either admin can cancel it.

gecolHlcCounts.title: GECOL / HLC counts
gecolHlcCounts.note: Read only. Counts the latest version of each record. Nothing here changes any data; it shows what is in the system before any move of GECOL or HLC data.

slaTasks.title: Tasks and their SLA
slaTasks.note: Every active task of the workflow in force and of the open draft is listed here. A task has an SLA, or it was explicitly marked as having none, or it is not decided yet. Nothing is decided for you.
slaTasks.banner_undecided: {{n}} tasks are not decided yet: set an SLA for them or mark them as having no SLA.
slaTasks.banner_ok: Every task has an SLA or an explicit "no SLA".
slaTasks.set_below: Set the SLA in the rule set below

issueMap.title: Issue category by task
issueMap.note: When a site is stopped, the category and the reason of its issue row follow the task where it is stopped. The list is filled from the task group and every line can be changed. The values come from the lists Issue category and Blocker reason.
issueMap.banner_unclassified: {{n}} tasks are not classified yet. Their issue rows show Other and Not classified.

recycleBin.title: Recycle bin
recycleBin.note: Voided register records can be restored for {{days}} days after they were voided. A restored record returns as a draft and goes through the workflow again. Nothing is deleted.
recycleBin.none: No voided record inside the retention window.
recycleBin.restore_note: The record returns as a draft (level 1). Its history and audit stay.
recycleBin.blocked_site_slot_taken: The site already has another record
recycleBin.audit_link: Every void and restore is in the audit log.

struct.title: Edit the structure through templates
struct.note: Download a register template, change the Structure sheet in Excel and upload it again. Nothing changes at once: the upload makes a proposal that a System Admin reviews and approves, and a new template version is issued when it is applied.
struct.download: Download the template with its Structure sheet
struct.approve_blocked: A blocked item stops the approval. Fix the value and upload again.
struct.revert_hint: The undo is a proposal of its own: it needs the same approval.
struct.two_people: This proposal changes a type or hides a column: a different System Admin must approve it.
struct.applied: The proposal was applied and a new template version is issued.
struct.uploaded: The proposal was made. Nothing is changed until it is approved.
struct.upload_hint: Only the Structure sheet is read. The data sheets are not.
struct.effect_new: New column: no data is affected
struct.block_new_column_incomplete: a new column needs a name and a type
struct.block_system_column: a column the system needs keeps its type, required flag and visibility
struct.block_conversion_blocked: some values do not convert to the new type
struct.block_unknown_list: the list does not exist or is inactive
struct.tab_note: Proposals made from a modified template or by the API for this register. Review each item and its effect on the data, then approve or reject.
struct.edit_link_hint: Open the structure changes of this register (Settings, Registers, Columns)

exportSchedules.title: Scheduled Master export
exportSchedules.note: A schedule does not run by itself in the background. When a schedule is due, the file is produced when you next open Exports (or the Exports list) in the app, with your own permissions at that moment. It then appears in your exports list. Only you see your schedules.
exportSchedules.name: Name
exportSchedules.due: Due, starts when you open Exports

motion.title: Motion
motion.note: One motion system for the whole app: dialogs, messages, cards, progress bars, charts and the map. This choice is saved in this browser, like the theme and the language.
motion.auto_note: Follow the operating system setting for reduced motion.
motion.reduced_note: No transitions or animations anywhere, including charts and the map.

seq.title: Numbering sequences
seq.note: The next number of each document type and form. A change applies to the numbers issued from now on; issued numbers never change.
seq.next_help: A whole number from 1. The database refuses a value that would repeat a number already issued.

matrixCoverage.title: Matrix coverage
matrixCoverage.note: Read only. Shows the cells of the Responsibility Matrix that nobody can act on, per row, region and level. Nothing here changes the matrix.
matrixCoverage.summary: {{ok}} covered, {{empty}} empty, {{nobody}} named but nobody active, of {{cells}} cells

sd.title: Time in each state
sd.note: Median and P85 working days of completed stays. Admin overrides are left out. Only the regions you can read are counted.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.view_hint: Sites on a date axis, read only
timeline.hint: Pick up to {{max}} date columns. Read only: dates change through their tasks.
timeline.empty_hint: Pick another date column or widen the filters.
timeline.note: {{shown}} of {{total}} loaded sites have a date in the chosen columns ({{all}} match the filters; the first 100 are drawn).

records.changed: Changed since you last opened it
records.pin_full: You can pin up to {{max}} records. Unpin one first.

loginPage.title: Login page
loginPage.note: What the sign-in page shows: the announcement, the background animation, the default language and the support links. Nothing here changes the sign-in mechanism.
loginPage.animation_note: A calm telecom network behind the sign-in pages. A visitor who prefers reduced motion never sees it.
loginPage.locale_note: Applies until the visitor picks a language once; their choice stays.
loginPage.links_note: Up to 5 links under the sign-in form (http, https or mailto).
loginPage.version_note: Shown to signed-in users only (the post-login screen). It is never on the public sign-in page.
loginPage.readonly: Only a System Admin, or a person they delegated settings to for all regions, can change this.
loginPage.confirm: Save the login page settings? The change is audited with your reason and shows on the sign-in page at once.

ui.guard_note: Ask before anything with unsaved input is closed or left: the choices are Save and leave, Discard and leave, or Stay.
ui.guard_settings_hint: Settings pages with edited, unsaved values
ui.guard_inline_hint: Site details and cells edited in place
ui.guard_navigation_hint: Links, the browser Back button and closing the tab
ui.avatars_note: A coloured avatar with the initials of a person, drawn by the system (no image is stored). It shows in the top bar and beside people in lists and tables.
ui.av_in_lists: Show avatars beside people in lists and tables
ui.new_note: A small badge beside a feature that now sits next to the older way to do the same thing.
ui.new_days: Days to show it after a feature is released
ui.new_preview: Shown beside new features until the days have passed.
ui.inbox_note: Tabs on the Inbox page and which kinds of notification count as priority. Priority items come first and carry a chip.
ui.inbox_tabs: Show tabs on the Inbox page
ui.inbox_priority_note: Mentions and approvals waiting are priority by default.
ui.panel_note: How the bell opens: a small popover, or a panel that slides in from the side with tabs.
ui.panel_tabs: Show the tabs (All, Unread, Priority) in the panel

goals.title: Goals
goals.settings_note: A goal counts the sites that reach a milestone task during the current month, quarter or year. The progress is counted from approved tasks, never typed. Each goal shows in the Goals card of the Dashboard.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.note: A passkey (fingerprint, face, screen lock or a security key) can replace the 6-digit code at the second step of the password sign-in. It adds nothing new to the sign-in: the code and the recovery codes keep working.
passkeys.enable: Let people use passkeys at the second step
passkeys.enable_note: Off by default. Only for accounts that already have two-step verification: nobody is forced to add one, and an account never ends up with a passkey only. Single Sign-On (Microsoft 365) accounts are not affected: their sign-in and second step belong to Microsoft.
passkeys.not_ready: The workspace web address (APP_BASE_URL, https) is not set on the server, so this cannot be turned on yet.
passkeys.recovery_note: Recovery: a System Admin can remove all passkeys of a person from the user page, and turning this off keeps the registered passkeys (they work again when it is turned back on). The code and the recovery codes work in every case.
passkeys.readonly: Only a System Admin can see and change the passkey setting.
passkeys.confirm_set: Passkeys will be {{state}}. This is recorded in the audit log.
passkeys.mine_note: Use a passkey instead of the 6-digit code when you sign in. Adding one asks you to confirm your password first. You can always use the code or a recovery code.
passkeys.remove_note: This passkey will stop working. Your code and recovery codes are not affected.
passkeys.label: Name for this passkey
passkeys.failed: The passkey could not be added.
passkeys.not_ready_user: Passkeys are not ready on this server yet. Ask a System Admin.
passkeys.needs_two_factor: Passkeys are an alternative to the code, so two-step verification must be on first.
passkeys.unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys.
passkeys.signin_failed: The passkey was not accepted. Use your code or a recovery code instead.
passkeys.revoke_note: Every passkey of this person is removed (for example a lost device). Their code and recovery codes are not touched, so they can still sign in.

newdevice.title: New-device code
newdevice.note: When this is on, a password-only sign-in from a browser the account has not used before needs a 6-digit code sent to the account's own email. It is off until you turn it on. Nothing is deleted, sessions already open keep working, and you can turn it off at any time.
newdevice.enable: Ask for an email code on a new device
newdevice.enable_note: Not asked of people with two-step verification (their authenticator is stronger), of System Admins (unless you include them), or of accounts with no email. If the code email cannot be queued the sign-in goes through, so nobody is locked out.
newdevice.no_mail: The mail server is not set up, so this cannot be turned on yet.
newdevice.admins_note: Leave this off so an admin can always sign in to turn the feature off or let someone in.
newdevice.readonly: Only a System Admin manages the new-device code.
newdevice.bypass: Let one person in without the code
newdevice.bypass_note: For someone who cannot reach their mailbox. It works for their next sign-in only, from any browser, for a few minutes.
newdevice.bypass_until: They can sign in once without the code until {{when}}.
newdevice.confirm_set: New-device code: {{enabled}}, valid {{minutes}} minutes. Your password is asked again and the change is written to the audit log.
newdevice.confirm_bypass: Let {{who}} sign in once without the code, for {{minutes}} minutes. It is written to the audit log.

devicecode.title: Check it is you
devicecode.body: This browser is new for your account. We sent a 6-digit code to your email. Enter it to finish signing in.
devicecode.label: Code from your email
devicecode.hint: 6 digits. It works once and expires soon.
devicecode.wrong: The code is not correct. Check your email and try again.

mySessions.title: My sessions
mySessions.note: The devices signed in as you. Sign out of any you do not recognise or no longer use. This device stays signed in; use Sign out for it.
mySessions.sign_out_others: Sign out of all other devices

matrixSimulate.title: Who approves?
matrixSimulate.note: Read only. Pick a site and a stage task or a register to see who would hold L1 and L2 today: the matrix cell that decides, its rule, the people who would hold the level and how they reach it (named, role, group). Nothing is written and nobody is notified. A task cell decides before the stage cell, and a region cell before the default cell.
matrixSimulate.fallback: Who could act through the admin path:

automation.title: Automation centre
automation.note: When something happens, tell the right people. Every automation here is an alert rule: the only action is a notification, and nothing is changed in any record, state or permission. The system runs them every day and writes each run to the Audit Log with no user.
automation.empty: No automation yet. Start from a template below.
automation.then_module: notify the people who work in {{module}}
automation.templates_note: A template creates a normal alert rule that you can edit afterwards in Manage rules.
automation.use_note: Creates the alert rule {{code}}, switched on. Say why you add it.
automation.runs_note: Runs are made by the system, not by a person.
automation.when_weekly_status_missing: a region has no weekly status update for the current week
automation.when_advance_unsettled: an advance stays unsettled for {{days}} days
automation.when_invoice_due_soon: an invoice is due within {{days}} days
automation.when_link_orphans: at least {{min}} row(s) of a register link point to a missing record

alertRules.title: Alert rules
alertRules.note: General if/then rules, notifications only. The daily job checks each enabled rule and sends one in-app notification per recipient, in their language. A rule never changes a record, a state or a holder.
alertRules.kind_weekly_status_missing_help: Fires for every region without a Weekly status update of the current working week. Placeholders: {{region}}.
alertRules.kind_advance_unsettled_help: Fires weekly for every approved advance still disbursed or in settlement for at least the days. Leave the days empty to use the Finance hub warning days. Placeholders: {{record}}, {{state}}, {{days}}.
alertRules.kind_invoice_due_soon_help: Fires once per invoice and due date for every approved invoice that is not paid or cancelled and is due within the days (7 when empty) or already late. Placeholders: {{record}}, {{due}}, {{days}}.
alertRules.kind_record_idle_help: Fires for every current record of the register in the state for at least the days. Placeholders: {{record}}, {{state}}, {{days}}.
alertRules.kind_kpi_threshold_help: Fires when the live KPI of the dashboard crosses the rule's own threshold. Placeholders: {{kpi}}, {{value}}, {{threshold}}.
alertRules.kind_link_orphans_help: Fires weekly for every declared register link that has at least the minimum rows (1 when empty) holding an id which is no current record of the target. Leave the register and field empty to check every link. Placeholders: {{register}}, {{field}}, {{target}}, {{count}}.

media.title: Media
media.sub: The photos and images of every enabled source in one gallery, read live from their records.
media.off: The Media gallery is switched off in Settings.
media.open_record: Open the record this file belongs to

mediaSet.title: Media gallery
mediaSet.note: What the Media tab of the library reads and how its thumbnails are made. Nothing is deleted: a switch only hides.
mediaSet.enabled_note: Off: the tab shows a notice and lists nothing.
mediaSet.kinds_note: Each document type has its own kind, allowed formats and photo rules. Change them in Document types.
mediaSet.types_link: Open Document types (kind, formats and rules per type)
mediaSet.image_only_note: Hide files that are not images (PDF, office files).
mediaSet.site_docs_note: Include slots that belong to a task or a site, not to a register.
mediaSet.withdrawn_note: Adds a Withdrawn filter to the tab. Withdrawn items are never deleted.
mediaSet.exclude_note: Codes of document types kept out of the gallery.
mediaSet.th_enabled_note: Made on first view and kept beside the original.
mediaSet.th_unavailable: The thumbnail maker is not installed on this server; cards show a type icon.
mediaSet.readonly: You can view these settings. A System Admin or a settings delegate changes them.
mediaSet.confirm: The change is audited with your reason.

unsaved.title: Unsaved changes
unsaved.body: You have changes that are not saved. What do you want to do?
unsaved.discard_hint: Leave without saving: the changes are lost
unsaved.reason_note: Saving a setting needs a reason (3 characters at least).
unsaved.save_failed: The changes could not be saved, so you are still here.

mailPolicy.title: Mail policy
mailPolicy.note: Who may be mailed. Notification mail goes to the person only for the kinds listed below in Mail notification kinds. Outside addresses stay off until you switch them on here.
mailPolicy.lock: The security lock that blocks public sharing is on: no mail goes to outside addresses while it is on.
mailPolicy.enabled: Notification mail is on (off stops all of it except security alerts)
mailPolicy.domains_note: An address whose domain is not listed is external. With no domain listed every address counts as internal.
mailPolicy.confirm_note: The change is audited and applies to the next mail.

oplimits.title: Operational limits
oplimits.note: The numbers the system keeps for itself: how long a sign-in lasts, how recent a password check must be, and how many rows one request or file may carry. Every value starts at the number the system always used, so nothing changes until you change one. Each change asks for your password again, needs a reason and is written to the audit log.
oplimits.session_idle_hours_hint: A session ends after this many hours without any activity. The person signs in again.
oplimits.session_absolute_hours_hint: A session ends this many hours after sign-in, even if the person is still working. It cannot be shorter than the idle sign-out.
oplimits.stepup_seconds_hint: Sensitive actions ask for the password again when the last check is older than this. A shorter window is safer and asks more often.
oplimits.assignments_max_rows_hint: Users times roles in one bulk assignment request. A larger request is refused with a message.
oplimits.import_max_rows_hint: Data rows accepted in one template file, list file or holiday file.
oplimits.master_import_max_rows_hint: Rows read from the Master sheet of one legacy import file.
oplimits.register_import_max_rows_hint: Rows read from each register sheet of one Master import file.
oplimits.prefill_max_rows_hint: Rows the system writes into a template it prefills with existing data.
oplimits.prefill_max_sites_hint: Sites taken from the Sites list filters when a template is prefilled.
oplimits.export_max_rows_hint: Audit log and security log exports are refused above this many rows; narrow the dates or export in parts.
oplimits.idempotency_max_entries_hint: How many recent requests the system remembers so a repeated click is not done twice. Older ones are dropped first.
oplimits.login_ip_attempts: Failed sign-ins per address before a wait
oplimits.login_ip_attempts_hint: One address may fail this many sign-ins inside the window below before every new attempt has to wait. Also the code and re-check attempts allowed per minute for one address or one account.
oplimits.login_ip_window_seconds_hint: Failures older than this are forgotten for the address.
oplimits.login_ip_base_seconds_hint: After the free failures, the first wait. It doubles on each further failure.
oplimits.login_ip_max_seconds_hint: The wait never grows past this. It cannot be shorter than the first wait. An address is never blocked for long, because many people share one.
oplimits.login_identifier_attempts_hint: Attempts allowed per minute for one account name, and for password re-checks and code regeneration.
oplimits.media_thumbnails_per_minute_hint: How many thumbnails one person can ask the Media gallery to make in a minute. A thumbnail that is already made is always shown and never counted. Above the limit the system answers "try again later" for a new thumbnail, and the original file is still available. 0 means no limit.
oplimits.registers_custom_max_hint: How many custom registers can be active at the same time. Hidden registers are not counted. Lowering it does not hide any register that already exists; it only stops new ones from being created.
oplimits.never: Never changed: every limit is at its default.
oplimits.readonly: Only a System Admin can change the limits.
oplimits.confirm: {{count}} limit(s) will differ from the default after this change. Your password is asked again and the change is written to the audit log.
oplimits.confirm_default: Every limit goes back to its default. Your password is asked again and the change is written to the audit log.
oplimits.bad_value: Use a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
oplimits.bad_session: The longest session cannot be shorter than the idle sign-out.
